title: Retention Register
constraints: An 8-bit register `q` in a switchable power domain, plus an always-on **shadow** register.

Each rising edge: while `pwr_on = 0`, `q` is lost (modelled as cleared to 0). Otherwise `restore` loads `q` from the shadow. Otherwise `en` loads `q` from `d`. Separately, `save && pwr_on` copies the **current** (pre-edge) `q` into the shadow. The shadow is never lost.
`q_out = pwr_on ? q : 0` (isolation). `rst` is an always-on synchronous reset that clears both `q` and the shadow.
hints: Two registers with different rules: the shadow only changes on `save`, while `q` is also destroyed when power is off.
Priority for `q`: power off > restore > enable.
Real retention flops put the shadow latch (balloon latch) on the always-on supply, and control it with SAVE/RESTORE pins driven by the power controller.

examples.title: retention
examples.input: q = 0x5A, save, pwr_on = 0, then pwr_on = 1 and restore
